issues.legal_issue: A finding on an issue in an earlier proceeding is binding in a later proceeding only when it was directly and substantially in issue, rather than merely collateral or incidental.
material_facts: The appeal concerned whether findings in earlier proceedings barred a later inquiry into whether the religious endowments were public trusts.
The earlier proceedings included a suit under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure and administrative inquiries under the public trusts law.
issues.conclusion: A finding on an issue that was only collateral or incidental in the earlier proceeding is not ordinarily res judicata; the court must determine whether the issue was necessary to the earlier decision and formed its substantive basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure distinguishes matters directly and substantially in issue from matters only collaterally or incidentally in issue. Applying the tests discussed in Mulla, the court said the pleadings, issues, and judgment must be examined to determine whether resolution of the issue was necessary and material to the decision. It relied on Ishwar Singh v. Sarwan Singh and Mohd. S. Labbai v. Mohd. Hanifa, and discussed Run Bahadur v. Lucho Koer, Asrar Ahmed v. Durgah Committee, Pragdasji v. Ishwarlal Bhai, Sulochana Amma v. Narayanan Nair, and Uthiva Somasundareswarar v. Rajanga as illustrations of the distinction.

predicates.prior_and_later_proceedings: A party relies on a finding from an earlier proceeding in a later proceeding.
predicates.issue_was_necessary_to_prior_decision: The earlier court had to decide the issue to adjudicate the principal matter before it.
predicates.prior_decision_rest_on_issue: The earlier decision rested substantively on its determination of the issue, rather than treating it as an auxiliary step in its reasoning.

issues.definition: When a finding from an earlier proceeding was necessary to its decision and that decision rested substantively on the finding, the finding is binding in the later proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A finding that an endowment was private in an earlier suit does not bar a later public-trust inquiry when the finding was incidental to the earlier suit and the governing statutory definition later encompasses the endowment's family-benefit purposes.
material_facts: An earlier suit under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure sought relief concerning the management of the shrines, including an injunction, a scheme, and appointment of trustees; the suit was dismissed.
The earlier court also found the endowment to be private, relying on the use of income for the maintenance of the religious office-holder, family members, and dependants.

The later inquiry arose under a public trusts statute whose definition of a public endowment included permanent dedication for pious purposes, including benefits for the settlor's family and the religious office-holder's family.
issues.conclusion: The earlier finding did not operate as res judicata in the later inquiry, both because the finding was not necessary to the earlier suit's decision and because the later statutory definition included endowments with the family-benefit feature on which the earlier finding had relied.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a declaration of public-trust status is not, by itself, one of the specified reliefs; under Pragdasji v. Ishwarlal Bhai, a finding on that status may be incidental when the suit fails on its substantive claims. The court also applied Section 2(19) of the Bombay Public Trusts Act, 1950, which includes permanent dedication for religious, charitable, or pious purposes, and agreed with Sayed Mohammed v. Ali Miya that family benefits of the kind described do not prevent an endowment from being a public trust under that definition.

rule.if: later_public_trust_inquiry and earlier_section_92_suit and earlier_status_finding_was_incidental and current_definition_includes_family_benefit_purposes

predicates.later_public_trust_inquiry: An authority is asked to determine whether an endowment is a public trust.
predicates.earlier_section_92_suit: An earlier suit sought relief concerning the administration of the endowment under a procedure limited to specified forms of relief.
predicates.earlier_status_finding_was_incidental: The earlier court addressed public or private status as an auxiliary matter rather than as a necessary substantive basis for its disposition of the suit.
predicates.current_definition_includes_family_benef: The law governing the later inquiry treats qualifying permanent dedication for pious purposes, including specified family benefits, as within the public-trust definition.

issues.definition: An incidental status finding in an earlier limited-relief suit does not bar a later public-trust inquiry when the governing definition includes the family-benefit purposes considered in the earlier case.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier decision between the parties ceases to control when a later decision between them determines the same matter to the contrary.
material_facts: An administrative decision held the endowment to be private and relied on an earlier judgment without considering the changed statutory definition.
A later High Court decision between the parties reached a contrary conclusion concerning the effect of the earlier judgment on a public-trust inquiry.
issues.conclusion: The earlier administrative decision did not operate as res judicata because the later contrary decision between the parties superseded it and governed.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the rule that an earlier decision binding between parties loses that force when a later decision between the same parties decides the matter to the contrary; the later decision then governs. It relied on Sayed Mohammed v. Ali Miya, which had considered the effect of the earlier judgment and the changed statutory definition.

predicates.later_proceeding_reconsiders_same_matter: A subsequent proceeding between parties addresses a matter previously decided.
predicates.earlier_decision_between_parties: An earlier decision determined that matter between the parties.
predicates.later_contrary_decision_between_parties: A later decision between the parties determined the same matter inconsistently with the earlier decision.

issues.definition: When a later decision between the parties determines the same matter contrary to an earlier decision, the later decision controls.

issues.legal_issue: A party cannot establish a res judicata bar in an appeal on the basis of an earlier proceeding when that ground was not raised in the proceedings below.
material_facts: The appellant relied on an earlier proceeding from 1965 as a basis for res judicata in the appeal.
The appellant had not raised a res judicata plea based on that proceeding in the lower courts.
issues.conclusion: The court rejected the res judicata contention based on the 1965 proceeding because the plea had not been raised in the lower courts.
issues.legal_principle: The court declined to decide the appeal on a res judicata ground that had not been raised in the lower courts. No earlier case was cited for this ruling.

predicates.appeal_challenges_rejection_of_res_judic: A party appeals after a lower court has rejected a res judicata objection.
predicates.earlier_proceeding_is_relied_on: The party relies on an earlier proceeding as the basis for the asserted bar.
predicates.res_judicata_ground_not_raised_below: The party did not raise that basis for res judicata in the lower courts.

issues.definition: On an appeal challenging rejection of a res judicata objection, a ground based on an earlier proceeding is rejected when the party did not raise it below.
